A hockey club records the number of people that watch each match. An 8-bit binary register is 1 used to store this value. 46 people watch the first match and 171 people watch the second match. (a) Show how the registers would store these denary values as 8-bit binary. Denary 8-bit binary value 46 171 [2] Working space Give the largest denary value that can be stored in the 8-bit binary register. (b) [1] The hockey club wants to increase the number of people that can watch each match to 2000. (c) The 8-bit binary register may no longer be able to store the value. Give the smallest number of bits that can be used to store the denary value 2000. [1] Working space

Electronic data about the final score for the match is transmitted to a central computer (d) 30 kilometres away, using serial transmission. Explain why serial transmission is more appropriate than parallel transmission in this (i) scenario. [3] The data transmission is also half-duplex. (ii) Describe half-duplex data transmission. [2] The data transmission uses checksums. (iii) Describe how checksums are used to detect errors in data transmission. [3]

Gurdeep takes high definition photographs using a digital camera. She has set up a website where 2 users can view thumbnails of her photographs. Describe how lossy compression creates the thumbnails. [3] Gurdeep sets up a web server to host her website.
